narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='m1'/>Three times one is three, so it is three point six five metres.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Each of the three strips has its own sixty five hundredths.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The slip counted that part only once, so the length came out far too short.
removed_beats.on_screen: the slip's bubble shows 3.65 m; three 0.65 m parts glow while only one is counted; 3.65 is struck through

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Write the decimal in hundredths and multiply by the counting number. Then change the answer back to a decimal.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Adding the three strips one after another gives the same length, so the answer checks out.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>A shirt maker can now cut the right amount for any number of shirts.
removed_beats.on_screen: the stage clears except the anchor; the words hundredths times a number appear; then the check 1.65 + 1.65 + 1.65 appears with a tick

old_misconception.wrong_move: A common slip multiplies only the one whole metre and keeps point six five, giving three point six five. Each shirt needs the point six five too.
